answer: Transaction-graph spectral clustering. Agents build a graph of pairwise interactions; sybils form dense, low-diversity clusters that stand out from the organic atlas of normal trade. Each identity must accumulate a minimum pigment of distinct counterparties before its activity counts. Penalty is retroactive: detected clusters forfeit all accrued reputation, and the operator's recovery cost scales with cluster size—roughly the full cost of re-establishing every member from a cold zenith.
